ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, this circuit is a transistor current amplification factor \(\beta\) test circuit. Suppose the transistor's \(U_{BE} = 0.7\,\text{V}\). If the voltmeter reading is 200 mV, then the value of \(\beta\) is ________.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a β test circuit composed of two ideal operational amplifiers A1, A2 and a transistor. The left-side +10 V power supply is connected through R1=3 kΩ to the node where the transistor collector is located, and at the same time this node is connected to A1; the other reference terminal of A1 is connected to +4 V, therefore according to ideal operational-amplifier negative feedback, this collector node is clamped at 4 V. In the right-side A2 part, R2=10 kΩ is fed back from the output terminal u0 to the transistor base/summing node, the voltmeter is connected between u0 and the reference terminal, and the reading is 200 mV; R3=10 kΩ is also marked in the figure. Reasoning: A1 makes the collector voltage 4 V, so the current flowing through R1, that is, the transistor collector current IC, is IC=(10 V−4 V)/3 kΩ=6 V/3000 Ω=2 mA. When A2 operates ideally, it makes the base/summing node approximately 0 V, therefore the voltage across R2 is equal to the voltmeter reading 200 mV. Thus the base current IB=200 mV/10 kΩ=0.2 V/10000 Ω=20 μA. The transistor current amplification factor β=IC/IB=2 mA/20 μA=100.

method.method_draft: First describe the figure: identify A1 with R1 = 3 kΩ between +10 V and the transistor collector node, with A1 referenced to +4 V; identify A2 with a 10 kΩ feedback resistor R2 from u0 to the transistor base node and a voltmeter measuring u0. Treat the op amps as ideal. A1 fixes the collector node at 4 V, giving IC = (10 − 4)/3 kΩ. A2 fixes the base/summing node near 0 V, so the voltmeter reading 200 mV across R2 corresponds to IB = 200 mV/10 kΩ. Compute β = IC/IB.
